Let
\[
K=\#\{i:X_i=1\}.
\]
Then
\[
X_1+\cdots+X_{12}=0 \iff K=6.
\]

First, we may assume the law is exchangeable: randomly permute the coordinates. This preserves unbiasedness, 8-wise independence, and the value of \(\mathbb P(K=6)\). So it is enough to optimize over distributions of \(K\in\{0,\dots,12\}\).

For any polynomial \(q(K)\) of degree at most \(8\), 8-wise independence implies
\[
\mathbb E q(K)=\mathbb E q(B),
\]
where \(B\sim \operatorname{Bin}(12,1/2)\), since \(K^d\) is a degree \(d\) polynomial in the indicators \(\mathbf 1_{X_i=1}\).

Now define
\[
q(k)=\frac{(k-1)(k-2)(k-3)(k-4)(k-8)(k-9)(k-10)(k-11)}{14400}.
\]
This has degree \(8\), and
\[
q(6)=1.
\]
Also, on \(k=0,1,\dots,12\), it is nonnegative except it is zero at
\[
1,2,3,4,8,9,10,11.
\]
In particular,
\[
q(k)\ge \mathbf 1_{\{k=6\}}
\]
for all \(k\in\{0,\dots,12\}\). Therefore
\[
\mathbb P(K=6)\le \mathbb E q(K)=\mathbb E q(B).
\]
Only \(k=0,5,6,7,12\) contribute to \(\mathbb E q(B)\). We have
\[
q(0)=q(12)=\frac{66}{5},\qquad q(5)=q(7)=\frac35,\qquad q(6)=1.
\]
Thus
\[
\mathbb E q(B)
=
\frac{2\cdot \frac{66}{5}+2\binom{12}{5}\cdot \frac35+\binom{12}{6}}{2^{12}}
=
\frac{2\cdot \frac{66}{5}+2\cdot 792\cdot \frac35+924}{4096}
=
\frac{297}{640}.
\]
So
\[
\mathbb P(K=6)\le \frac{297}{640}.
\]

It remains to show this is attainable. Define an exchangeable distribution by choosing \(K\) with probabilities

\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}
k&1&2&3&4&6&8&9&10&11\\
\hline
\mathbb P(K=k)&\frac9{2240}&\frac{33}{1792}&\frac{11}{448}&\frac{99}{448}&\frac{297}{640}&\frac{99}{448}&\frac{11}{448}&\frac{33}{1792}&\frac9{2240}
\end{array}
\]
and then, conditional on \(K=k\), choose uniformly among all sign vectors with exactly \(k\) entries equal to \(1\).

These probabilities sum to \(1\). Let \(S=X_1+\cdots+X_{12}=2K-12\). By symmetry all odd moments vanish, and direct calculation gives
\[
\mathbb E S^2=12,\quad
\mathbb E S^4=408,\quad
\mathbb E S^6=21792,\quad
\mathbb E S^8=1532928.
\]
These are exactly the corresponding moments of a sum of \(12\) independent unbiased \(\{-1,1\}\)-variables.

For an exchangeable \(\{-1,1\}\)-vector, the averages of products over \(j\)-subsets are elementary symmetric polynomials in the coordinates, hence polynomials in \(S\) of degree \(j\). Therefore matching the moments of \(S\) through degree \(8\) gives
\[
\mathbb E\prod_{i\in A}X_i=0
\]
for every nonempty \(A\) with \(|A|\le 8\). Thus the construction is unbiased and 8-wise independent.

In this construction,
\[
\mathbb P(X_1+\cdots+X_{12}=0)=\mathbb P(K=6)=\frac{297}{640}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{297}{640}}
\]
